title: Man killed in London police shooting identified as 29-year-old from Lambton County
subtitle: A man fatally shot during a confrontation with London police in a downtown alley is a 29-year-old from Lambton County, Ontario's police watchdog says.
article: London police responded Thursday around 3:45 a.m. to a break-in near St. George and Mill streets. An officer saw a suspect in an alley on Richmond Row, where there was "an interaction" and an officer fired their gun at the man, the Special Investigations Unit (SIU) said.
London police said two officers were involved in the interaction, one of whom was injured but has since been released from the hospital.
The deceased is a 29-year-old man from Lambton County , SIU spokesperson Kristy Denette said Friday.
"His next of kin declined to release his name," Denette added in an email.
The watchdog is investigating the actions of one officer and 14 officers have been designated witnesses, the SIU said.
The SIU probes all cases of death, serious injuries, allegations of sexual assault and gunfire involving police officers.
The London police board, the civilian body that oversees policing, released a statement Friday.

"The board extends their support and hope for a full and fast recovery to the two officers directly involved and to all affected by this tragic incident, and sends their condolences to the loved ones of the deceased," the board said.
On Friday, London police and SIU investigators had cleared the scene behind a plaza at Richmond and Pall Mall streets where the shooting happened.

Citing a policy of not commenting on SIU probes, London police aren't providing any additional information about the break-in call that brought police to the area that is home to many Western University students.

Two women who live in a home at the corner of Mill and St. George streets told The London Free Press police showed up at their home around 4 a.m. and told them they were looking for three suspects spotted outside the home with a ladder and tools.
A man seen speaking with a police officer outside the home later Thursday morning told The Free Press he had tried to steal a street sign and brought a ladder and tools from his nearby home.
The man, who said he was joined by two other men, ran away after seeing flashing police lights and hearing sirens, he said.
"While running away, I heard the shots," he said.
